I apologize for the search issues. Let me analyze this question based on my knowledge about Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS).

Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS), now commonly known as Safety Data Sheets (SDS), are documents that contain important information about hazardous substances. They are required by workplace health and safety regulations in many countries.

An MSDS typically includes:

1. Identification of the substance/mixture and of the company/undertaking
2. Hazards identification (all hazards regarding the material)
3. Composition/information on ingredients
4. First-aid measures
5. Fire-fighting measures
6. Accidental release measures
7. Handling and storage (precautions for safe handling and storage)
8. Exposure controls/personal protection
9. Physical and chemical properties
10. Stability and reactivity
11. Toxicological information
12. Ecological information
13. Disposal considerations
14. Transport information
15. Regulatory information
16. Other information

Looking at the options provided in the question:
A. All hazards regarding the material - Yes, this is included in the "Hazards identification" section
B. Physical and chemical properties - Yes, this is included in the "Physical and chemical properties" section
C. Precautions for safe handling and storage - Yes, this is included in the "Handling and storage" section

Since all three options are correct information found on an MSDS, the answer includes all of them.
